name: SpikingLM
tagline: Bringing language understanding to fully spiking computation.
overview: SpikingLM addresses two obstacles in deep spiking language models: inactive neurons that weaken gradients, and the loss of token competition when Softmax is removed. It combines Distribution-aware Scaling with Spike2Max to improve training and attention while retaining efficient computation.
method: Rescales linear outputs into a range that supports neuron activity and gradient propagation. The scaling parameters can be fused into the preceding linear layers for inference.
Restores competition between tokens using base-2 exponentiation and max-subtraction, enabling efficient bit-shift operations.
results: lower energy consumption reported in the paper's evaluation
energy reduction for Spike2Max compared with Softmax
resultNote: The paper evaluates language understanding on GLUE. See the paper for model configurations, energy assumptions and comparisons.

name: AGMM
tagline: More stable learning for accurate binary spiking networks.
overview: Binary spiking networks combine event-driven computation with compact synaptic weights. AGMM investigates frequent weight sign flipping as a training bottleneck and adapts gradient magnitudes to improve learning stability.
method: Analyze how repeated changes in binary weight signs interfere with learning.
Modulate gradients during training to reduce unnecessary weight sign changes and improve convergence.
results: reported relative to the binary spiking baselines evaluated in the paper
evaluation on both conventional image and event-based datasets
resultNote: The experiments report improved binary-network accuracy and a narrower gap to full-precision counterparts. Detailed settings and comparisons are available in the paper.

name: BSO
tagline: Online optimization for binary weights with less training memory.
overview: BSO reduces the memory burden of training binary spiking networks by updating binary weights directly. Its temporal-aware variant, T-BSO, uses gradient information across time steps to adjust the update threshold.
method: Flip a binary weight when the product of gradient momentum and the weight crosses a threshold, removing the need to maintain latent weights.
T-BSO incorporates temporal gradient information into adaptive threshold selection.
results: direct weight updates within an online training framework
formal regret bounds for BSO and T-BSO
resultNote: The paper reports improved optimization performance over the evaluated binary spiking training methods. Consult its experiments for accuracy and memory comparisons.
